reason: Moving the cloud to the outskirts is the only offered gameplay action and may show where it goes.

effect: The outer cloud is drawn outward by the approaching galaxy’s unequal pull, completing the gas goal without a collision.
reaction: I liked that the cloud had a different fate from either colliding gas portion.

mostWorthwhile.text: The dense-gas collision was most worthwhile: its contrast with stars passing between one another made the different physical outcomes clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: Moving the outer cloud was the least engaging decision because it was the only gameplay action offered, although its result added useful context.

surprise.text: The thin gas formed a hot bridge instead of collapsing promptly into stars, unlike the denser gas that gathered further.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt especially arbitrary; the outer-cloud move had a clear destination, even if its eventual outcome was uncertain.

continue.text: Yes. The contrasting fates of stars and gas made me curious about how the cloud might eventually form new stars and worlds.
